# Human-Infective RNA Viruses

> A searchable atlas of the 239 RNA virus species with documented human infection,
> built from the open catalogue of Zhang et al. Each record carries ICTV taxonomy, transmission
> level, transmission routes and vector, host range, and the year and country of the first
> reported human infection. First reports span 1901 to 2022.

Site: https://curtishoffmann.com/human_infective_rna_viruses/
Maintainer: Curtis Hoffmann (https://curtishoffmann.com)
Source repository: https://github.com/phagehunter/human_infective_rna_viruses
Page built: 2026-10-24

## The data

Every record derives from one upstream release, committed to the repository unchanged:

- Dataset: Zhang F, Lu L, Brierley L, Hietanen H, Woolhouse MEJ. Human-infective RNA virus
  database. figshare, version 2. doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.30094726.v2. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
- Paper: Zhang F, Lu L, Brierley L, Hietanen H, Woolhouse MEJ. A complete catalogue of
  human-infective RNA viruses. Scientific Data. 2026;13:981. doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07281-5
- Risk scores: SpillOver: Viral Risk Ranking (spillover.global), covering 33 of these species.

Anyone citing the catalogue should cite Zhang et al., not this site.

## Shape of the catalogue

- 239 species across 23 families and 61 genera
- 57 countries of first report, 5 genome types
- First human reports from 1901 to 2022

### Transmission level

The level describes how far a virus travels between people. It is not a severity scale.

- Level 2: 147 species — limited onward transmission between humans
- Level 3: 32 species — longer chains of transmission between humans
- Level 4a: 36 species — sustained human-to-human transmission, with an animal reservoir
- Level 4b: 24 species — sustained human-to-human transmission, no animal reservoir needed

### Largest families

- Flaviviridae: 31 species
- Picornaviridae: 25 species
- Togaviridae: 22 species
- Peribunyaviridae: 21 species
- Rhabdoviridae: 19 species
- Paramyxoviridae: 17 species
- Hantaviridae: 14 species
- Arenaviridae: 12 species
- Retroviridae: 11 species
- Phenuiviridae: 10 species
- Sedoreoviridae: 9 species
- Nairoviridae: 8 species

## Limits a reader should know

- The catalogue records human infection, not disease burden, severity or current circulation.
- A blank transmission route or host means no recorded evidence, not evidence of absence.
- 32 records carry no reference sequence accession.
- 206 records have no SpillOver risk score.
- 48 records carry a cell the source marks with an asterisk whose
  meaning the dataset does not define; the value is shown as recorded and the mark is kept.
- Coordinates are the locality of first report and are not plotted, because
  65 records share a point with at least one other.

See DATA.md in the repository for the checksum, the normalization report and the full provenance.
